name: Vili, ALGAB site B503
catalog_citation: Alewijnse, Bart, John Nerbonne, Lolke J. van der Veen & Franz Manni. 2007. A computational analysis of Gabon varieties. In Proceedings of the RANLP Workshop on Computational Phonology, Borovetz, pp. 3-12. Author PDF (10 pp., TeX text layer), https://www.let.rug.nl/nerbonne/papers/Alewijnse-et-al-gabon-2007.pdf.
catalog_locator: PDF p. 2, section 3 'Data', 3.1 'Summary', left column (proceedings pagination not recoverable from the author copy). Site B503 Vili appears on PDF pages 5,9,10 (sampling map, consensus dendrogram beside B51/B52/B53, and the appendix row 'B503 Vili no code available (not listed as such)' on p. 10).
catalog_quote: Although tone and stress information have been ignored in this study, the authors do not assume these features to be less relevant, only that both require a fuller treatment after more careful study. Stress is not marked in the database because it is predictable in all varieties. It is usually placed systematically on the first syllable on the noun stem, while sometimes straightforward penultimate stress is used. No stress contrasts have been found (within single varieties). While the decision not to mark stress is understandable from the point of phonological theory, we would prefer to have data marked with stress to keep track of its distinctive use among different varieties. As far as we know, tone is indeed distinctive in most if not all varieties. Previous analysis has revealed a few different basic categories of tone systems in use ... Since tone has not been systematically transcribed in the field (for different reasons, including absence of tonal contrast at the surface, and because of the priority given to the segmental level, or due to the ability of the consultant), tonal information had to be discarded from the data in this analysis for ease of comparison.

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for vili1239, so this is the first stress statement held by the project. It is a database-wide generalization by the ALGAB fieldworkers (van der Veen co-author) covering the B503 Vili site, not a description of Ivili itself; it supports 'predictable, non-contrastive stress, usually stem-initial, in a tone language' but cannot fix Vili's placement between stem-initial and penultimate.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Blanket statement over all 53 ALGAB Gabon sampling sites (B503 Vili among them): word stress is predictable and non-contrastive; it usually falls on the first syllable of the noun stem, though some (unnamed) varieties instead have plain penultimate stress; tone is distinctive in most if not all of the varieties. The paper does not say which pattern B503 Vili follows.
new_statements.exceptions: 'sometimes straightforward penultimate stress is used' in some varieties (not identified); the authors note absence of surface tonal contrast in some data as one reason tone was not transcribed. No Vili-specific detail.
new_statements.identity_note: The paper's site 'B503 Vili' (appendix: 'B503 Vili no code available (not listed as such)') is the ALGAB wordlist point for the Gabonese inland Vili (Ivili) — per the prior check of Van der Veen 2014, the ALGAB list is 'B503 vili de Sindara' — i.e. Vili of Ngounie, not the coastal Vili (H12, ISO vif). In the paper's consensus dendrogram B503 groups with B53 (Poungi), B52 and B51, consistent with the B50 affiliation of this variety. The stress statement itself is not variety-specific: it is asserted for 'all varieties' in the 53-site ALGAB database.
